blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why a sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one? The answer lies in the concept of pressure.

blocks.markdown: Pressure is a measure of how much force is applied over a certain area. It is an important concept in physics, especially when dealing with fluids like water and air.

blocks.title: Definition of Pressure
blocks.text: Pressure is defined as the force exerted per unit area. The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

blocks.markdown: The formula for calculating pressure is given by $P = \frac{F}{A}$, where $P$ is the pressure, $F$ is the force applied, and $A$ is the area over which the force is distributed.

blocks.title: Calculating Pressure
blocks.prompt: A force of 50 N is applied to an area of 2 m². Calculate the pressure exerted.

steps.text: Identify the given values: Force $F = 50 \text{ N}$, Area $A = 2 \text{ m}^2$.
Use the formula $P = \frac{F}{A}$ to calculate pressure.

blocks.markdown: In fluids, pressure also depends on the depth and density of the fluid. The pressure in a liquid is given by $P = \rho gh$, where $\rho$ is the density of the liquid, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity, and $h$ is the height of the liquid column.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that pressure in a fluid increases with depth. This is why deep-sea divers need special equipment to withstand high pressures.

points: Pressure is the force per unit area, measured in pascals (Pa).
In fluids, pressure increases with depth and is calculated using $P = \rho gh$.
